newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks finish strongly in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks finish strongly in heavy trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks climbed 1.67 percent to a much higher close on Monday, lifted by positive sentiment surrounding the property and finance sectors and underpinned by a rebound on Wall Street, brokers said.
"The market's momentum derives in large part from Wall Street's 100-point rebound on Friday," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The Hang Seng Index jumped 221.14 points to end at the day high of 13,443.93. Turnover was a robust HK$11.13 billion, slightly higher than Friday's HK$11.09 billion.
The index's advance came despite the suspension of three large index constituents and continued selling in CITIC Pacific.
On Friday, the Dow rose 101.60 points or nearly 1.6 percent to 6,544.09, with investors becoming more confident the U.S. economy was going to grow at a moderate rate.
Trading in shares of Cheung Kong, Hutchison Whampoa and Hongkong Electric and Cheung Kong Infrastructure (CKI) was suspended on Monday after the announcement of a major corporate reshuffle.
Hutchison plans to make a general offer for Hongkong Electric and then transfer its stake in the utility to Cheung Kong Infrastructure (CKI) in exchange for new CKI shares.
Cheung Kong will transfer its existing holding in CKI, equal to 70.66 percent of CKI's issued capital, to Hutchison.
Based on Hutchison's Friday closing price of HK$58.50 and CKI's of HK$21.15, Hutchison will pay for the CKI shares by issuing 349.5 million new shares to parent Cheung Kong.
"We are recommending 'buys' for Cheung Kong and Hutchison and 'sells' for CKI and Hongkong Electric," said Archie Hart in institutional sales at BZW Securities.
The property sector led the market, followed by utilities.

Sun Hung Kai Properties gained HK$1.50 to HK$95.75 and New World Development put on HK$1.50 to HK$53.75. China Light leaped HK$1.50 to HK$35.50, while Hongkong and China Gas rose HK$0.30 to HK$15.10. HSBC Holdings climbed HK$3.00 to HK$168.00.
CITIC Pacific was the most active issue on turnover of HK$1.25 billion. The share slumped HK$2.40 to HK$40.20.
"Investors are confused about the deal," said BZW's Hart, referring to parent CITIC Hong Kong's decision to sell 15.47 percent of the listed company to a management team.
